summary: Recent disputes over naming conventions at major D.C. institutions have highlighted questions about who holds authority over the District's landmarks and public spaces, while a senator has pledged to prioritize statehood legislation. Without statehood, D.C. residents have no voting representation in Congress, and Congress can override any law the District passes.
